summary: All three occurrences were checked. The two k/ko-marked forms belong to Infectum even where the edition uses past progressive; sayġiwa belongs to Infectum-wa.
Roof fencing for defense remains the existing umzäunen meaning. Fortifying expresses the context's purpose; no separate military technical sense is required.

Kosayġila indexes the feminine roof with -la and specifies b-marked briars; kosayġina has a zero-marked roof patient. The 215 -wa clause is already the recording quotation in the entry and is not duplicated.
The current parsed Infectum-wa box contains one example. A recording citation is not a second example; the reader's older count does not require a structural correction.
The existing Preterit wood-arranging quotation is retained unchanged; the supplied roof occurrences do not establish whether its organizing meaning deserves a separate sense.
Does the inherited səġli aq qayse quotation denote stacking/arranging wood independently of fencing? Its English paraphrase is wider than umzäunen, but no new matching occurrence is supplied here.
Confirm whether roof fortification with briars is always described by ordinary fencing or also by a conventional defensive meaning. Current evidence does not justify splitting it.
